newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Central Bank aiming to lower bank costs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Central Bank aiming to lower bank costs.

text.p: The President of the Argentine Central Bank, Pedro Pou, said Monday now that the country has achieved the goal of low inflation his institution is set to work towards reducing costs in the banking sector.

"Having achieved the objective of price stability, we should focus our work on the efficiency of the banking industry, with the objective of achieving banking costs similar to international levels," Pou said at a bankers conference in Buenos Aires.
Since the introduction of Convertibility in Argentina in 1991, fixing the value of the peso to the dollar at par, inflation has all but disappeared.
As late as 1990, Argentina suffered from annual inflation in excess of 1,000 percent. Last year it rose just five percent.

Pou said the stability of recent years had made it possible for lending rates to fall consistently. "But this drop is not sufficient, since as I have said we aspire to reach levels similar to international ones," said Pou.

He said one of the reasons why rates continue to be high in Argentina is the still low level of bank deposits in the country. Among things the bank is doing to improve this is the introduction of a new payments settlement system.
It is hoped the new system will reduce inter-bank payments and lead to the introduction of new bank services, said Pou.

Another step taken by the bank is the introduction of a system with centralized information on debtors. The lack of an information system on the credit worthiness of borrowers has led to higher borrowing costs across the board because those that do not meet their obligations have increased service costs for banks in Argentina.

Finally, Pou said: "The financial system today is in condition not only to play its part in supporting exchange stability but also to contribute, in a growing way, to improving the efficiency of the process of transforming savings into productive investment."
